BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Executive view

The Seller’s package materially departs from Wattlebridge’s playbook. The “STANDARD,” “FINAL,” and “agreed” labels, market-practice assertions, and request to focus only on “[OPEN]” items do not change our instructions. We should review the whole package against the playbook and should not treat any of these positions as agreed without the required buyer authority.

The principal pushbacks are the general warranty cap and thresholds, claim period, treatment of fundamental/title claims, disclosure and knowledge bars, Bluefen and Riverlark completion protections, and the unitemised employee bonuses. Tax and IP remain open; the Seller’s assertion that they are settled is not a resolution.

## Issues and recommended positions

### 1. General warranty cap

The Seller proposes AUD 4.8 million, or 20% of the AUD 24 million price. Our opening position is **25%, or AUD 6 million**.

Reject the proposed 20% cap unless Amelia Frost gives **prior written authority identifying the draft**. No such approval has been given. Do not describe 20% as an agreed fallback or accept it through markup, correspondence, or conduct.

### 2. De minimis and basket

The proposed AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping point basket are both above our positions: **AUD 5,000 de minimis** and **AUD 50,000 aggregate basket**, with recovery **from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded**.

Push back on both amounts and the Seller’s excess-only recovery approach. Confirm the drafting does not turn the basket into a deductible or apply it to categories that the playbook keeps outside the general regime.

### 3. Claim period and scope of limitations

The Seller proposes 18 months for general warranty claims. Our position is **24 months after Completion**. Eighteen months is available only with Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given.

Reject the proposed default that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly disapplied. That risks extending general limitations across distinct claim types by silence. Draft separate regimes for general, fundamental/title, Tax, IP, payment, and covenant claims, and state clearly which rules apply to each.

### 4. Fundamental and Title claims

The Seller would put capacity and title claims under the general cap and time limits. That conflicts with our required separate regime: **100% cap and at least six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

Insist on that separate regime. Also require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal share-register record; it is not independent proof and should not be treated as completing our verification.

### 5. Fraud, deliberate misconduct, remedies and reliance

The Seller seeks to apply limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions to all Claims. Reject any drafting that captures fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. Those matters must be carved out of **all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions**, to the maximum extent enforceable, and are not waivable under the playbook.

Check the operative clauses, not just the Seller Update summary, for conflicting or indirect overrides.

### 6. Disclosure framework

The Disclosure Letter purports to disclose every matter in the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Reject blanket or deemed disclosure of that kind. Require **specific fair disclosure**: a matter should qualify a warranty only where the letter identifies it with sufficient detail to enable the Buyer to understand its nature and scope.

The individual disclosures should be assessed on their actual terms. For example:

- **Bluefen:** DD-002 records a customer representing about 30% of FY26 revenue and a consent clause with conditions. The letter expressly says final consent and evidence of satisfied conditions are absent. This is not a basis to treat the condition as met.
- **Riverlark:** DD-003 records about AUD 3.2 million outstanding and no repayment or final security discharge. General disclosure does not solve the payoff or release requirement.
- **Ironquay:** DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010’s AUD 180,000 open amount is not independent verification of non-payment, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is disclosed.
- **Bonuses:** DD-005 identifies conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, but does not address applicable on-costs or put the amounts in the funds flow.
- **Incident:** DD-006 describes a preliminary investigation and unresolved access, scope and notification questions. It does not establish a confirmed breach or quantified loss.
- **Supplier renewals:** DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together. The AUD 330,000 total alone does not establish that the renewals are unavoidable, accrued, non-terminable or outside the ordinary course.
- **Title:** DD-012 identifies the source of the Seller’s title assertion; it does not establish independent verification.

### 7. Buyer knowledge

The proposed exclusion for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers—including matters discoverable from the data room or public records—is a blanket knowledge bar. Delete it.

If a knowledge qualifier is retained for any relevant warranty, limit it to specifically named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never qualify title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Data-room access or what a prudent search might reveal is not a substitute for specific fair disclosure.

### 8. Bluefen consent

The consent is material given the customer’s reported revenue contribution and the contractual change-control clause. “Reasonable endeavours” alone is insufficient, and consent must not be deemed satisfied merely on delivery of a written consent.

Require **effective consent and evidence that its conditions have been satisfied before Completion**. If those requirements are not met, the agreement should not treat the condition as fulfilled.

### 9. Riverlark facility and security release

A release to be provided after Completion leaves the Buyer exposed to an outstanding facility and unreleased security. Require a current payout figure, repayment directly from Completion funds, and effective security releases.

Do not accept a post-Completion release as the ordinary solution. Any such structure requires an **irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval**.

### 10. Employee bonuses and funds flow

DD-005 identifies AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses, with possible payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs not quantified. The draft funds flow omits them.

Require the bonuses and triggered on-costs to be a **specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded**. Do not allow them to be silently excluded or treated as an unexamined Company liability. Confirm how the agreed debt-free/cash-free price mechanics apply, without assuming a price deduction that has not been agreed.

### 11. Ironquay IP

The Seller’s position preserves only the existing narrow SOW3 payment indemnity. Our instruction is to **broaden the indemnity**, while preserving the SOW3 cure. Address the risk that payment conditions affect transfer of the Project Materials, and require appropriate evidence or a workable cure mechanism.

The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way. Do not assert it is unpaid as an established fact, but do not treat the Seller’s disclosure as proof of payment or assignment. Tax and IP terms remain open; the Seller’s statement that they are settled should be rejected.

### 12. Export/privacy incident

Keep the DD-006 position neutral. The record supports an unintended delivery and a preliminary investigation; it does **not** establish a confirmed breach, access by an unauthorised person, harm, a notification duty, or a numeric demand.

Require preservation of relevant logs and evidence, a proper investigation, and updates. Do not assume either that a notification or remediation obligation has been triggered or that the incident is immaterial.

### 13. Sandbar renewals

The three renewals total AUD 330,000, but the disclosure does not establish their timing, scope, avoidability, termination rights, accrual or ordinary-course status. Assess those matters in diligence and against the agreed price mechanics.

Do not automatically classify the amount as Debt or deduct it from the price; equally, do not accept the Seller’s unsupported characterisation as ordinary-course operating costs.

### 14. Lease, Mossvale and other stated disclosures

The disclosures say the office lease contains a notification obligation, but not that landlord consent is required for the share sale. The Mossvale assignment restriction likewise does not state that consent is required merely because shares are sold. Check the underlying terms and obtain any notice or consent actually required; do not infer a consent requirement from these summaries alone.

## Summary of recommendations

1. Restore the **25% general cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket with first-dollar recovery, and 24-month general claim period**. Do not accept the Seller’s lower figures without the specified Amelia Frost approval.
2. Give **fundamental/title claims a separate 100% cap and at least six years**, outside the general thresholds and knowledge bar; obtain independent title evidence.
3. Reject blanket data-room, public-register and buyer-knowledge exclusions; require specific fair disclosure and narrowly controlled knowledge qualifiers.
4. Preserve broad carve-outs for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct across all relevant limitations and remedy provisions.
5. Make Bluefen consent and satisfied conditions a genuine pre-Completion requirement; repay Riverlark directly from Completion funds and obtain effective releases.
6. Put the bonuses and triggered on-costs in the funds flow or have the Seller fund them; broaden the Ironquay indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.
7. Investigate and monitor DD-006 without assuming an unproven breach or loss; assess Sandbar on its actual terms without automatic Debt treatment or price adjustment.
8. Keep Tax and IP open and review the full operative SPA for cross-category overrides; the Seller’s labels and summaries are not a substitute for clause-by-clause review.
